data.title: Zee Entertainment buyback to open on Dec 1, set to close on Dec 7
data.description:
Zee Entertainment Enterprises will open its share buyback offer on December 1 and close it on December 7, according to a stock exchange filing by the company on Friday.
 
The company submitted its letter of offer and the tender forms for the proposed buyback to the stock exchanges.
 
Under the buyback, Zee Entertainment plans to buy back up to 65.93 million fully paid-up equity shares with a face value of ₹1 each. The total buyback size is capped at ₹600 crore. The buyback price is ₹91 per share, and the company's share price closed 1.5 per cent higher at ₹67.05 on Friday.
 
 
On November 12, the board of the company approved the buyback.
 
The buyback will be conducted through the tender offer route, allowing eligible shareholders to tender their shares in accordance with the terms set out in the letter of offer.
 
Shareholders wishing to participate in the buyback must submit their completed tender forms and other specified documents to the registrar by December 7, the last date of the offer.
 
The settlement of bids on the stock exchanges is scheduled to be completed by December 14.

data.title: Cabinet clears fresh women's reservation Bill with 50% seat rise formula
data.description:
The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation Constitution Amendment Bill. While copies of the Bill were yet to be circulated among lawmakers, government sources asserted that the fresh Bill hard-coded in its text a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats for all states. The formula, they said, would assuage the concerns of the southern states and help pave the way for its passage in the special session of Parliament next week.
 
In April, the government had insisted that no state’s share of seats in the Lok Sabha would decline, but did not include any such guarantee in the text of the Bill. The Bill fell 54 votes short of the two-thirds mark, which is required for the passage of a constitutional amendment. But the arithmetic has changed since that defeat nearly eight months ago.
 
 
The split in the Trinamool Congress led to 20 of its Lok Sabha MPs joining the fledgling Nationalist Citizens Party of India, which is now a constituent of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). Six of the Shiv Sena (UBT)’s MPs joined the Shiv Sena, and the return of the Shiromani Akali Dal, which has one Lok Sabha MP, to the NDA has increased the NDA’s numbers.
 
There were indications on Friday evening that the government's proposal of a 50 per cent increase in seats for all states based on the 1971 Census, and delimitation based on the 2011 Census, could persuade the Congress’ current and former allies, particularly the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), which has eight Lok Sabha MPs, and the DMK, which has 22 Lok Sabha MPs. The two parties had helped defeat a similar Bill during the hastily convened special session in mid-April this year. There were also fears in the Opposition camp that several of its MPs could be absent on the day of voting on the Bill.
 
The Congress convened a meeting of its INDIA (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance) bloc for Saturday morning and invited former ally DMK. Its Parliamentary Strategy Group held a meeting on Friday evening, and the party later alleged that the ultimate objective of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was the gerrymandering of constituencies, as was done in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir, in the garb of women’s reservation. The party said the BJP has “treated the Election Commission like a puppet”, and a delimitation exercise will follow a similar course.
 
In Chennai, DMK president M K Stalin said that under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18 per cent share of seats in the Lok Sabha be reduced. He also hit out at the Congress party, which joined the TVK alliance and the government led by it after the DMK was defeated in the Assembly polls held earlier this year. NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule said she would not attend the INDIA bloc’s meeting on Saturday as her father, Sharad Pawar, was ailing, but another leader said the party would support the Bill.
 
The proposed amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The treasury benches said the move would pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies ahead of the 2029 general election. The fresh Bill seeks to use the 2011 Census to redraw constituencies following the increase in seats. The Cabinet meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth. The government has called for a four-day special sitting — November 30 and December 1 in the Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in the Rajya Sabha.
 
At a press conference in New Delhi, Independent Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal appealed to Opposition parties to ensure that the delimitation Bill includes a provision that, instead of a single retired judge, there should be a retired judge nominated by the government and another nominated by the Opposition, with both together choosing a third judge to form a three-member delimitation panel. Sibal also highlighted the delay in the case seeking the disqualification of TMC and Shiv Sena (UBT) rebels. Sibal claimed that Parliament would be "defanged", with no debates or transparency. Between April and now, the BJP has used all its might and persuasive power through agencies and other means to persuade some members who are part of the Opposition to agree to this formula, he claimed.
 
(With inputs from Agencies)

data.title: Gavai writes to President, flags community bias in judicial appointments
data.description:
Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) B R Gavai has raised concerns over alleged community-based considerations in appointments and transfers of judges to constitutional courts, urging President Droupadi Murmu to intervene to uphold diversity, inclusivity, and merit in the judicial appointments process.
 
In a three-page letter dated November 27, Justice Gavai questioned the functioning of the Supreme Court Collegium, alleging that its recent recommendations appeared to favour members of a particular community at the expense of candidates from marginalised backgrounds.
 
Without identifying the community, the former CJI said a group accounting for less than 5 per cent of the country's population now constitutes more than 40 per cent of the Supreme Court's strength, with its representation having increased substantially in recent years.
 
 
While acknowledging that such disparities were not new, Gavai said the situation had become increasingly difficult to overlook.
 
He also expressed concern that candidates from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, and minorities, as well as women, were being overlooked when they did not belong to the community allegedly receiving preferential consideration.
 
Clarifying that he was not opposed to the representation of any section of society, Gavai said his efforts had consistently been directed towards maintaining a balance among different sections.
 
However, he alleged that recent developments suggested that recommendations were increasingly being influenced by considerations of appeasing a particular community.
 
The letter also questioned the rationale behind certain recommendations involving the transfer and elevation of high court chief justices.
 
Citing one instance, Justice Gavai referred to a chief justice who had previously been transferred twice to progressively smaller high courts but was subsequently recommended for appointment as the chief justice of a prominent high court. The recommendation, he alleged, appeared to have been made because of the judge's community background. The transfer of another meritorious and hardworking chief justice to a smaller high court was allegedly intended to facilitate the move.
 
Gavai said such decisions were demoralising for the affected judges and could adversely impact judicial officers, particularly those belonging to marginalised sections.
 
He also questioned how a judge who had been repeatedly transferred on punitive grounds, without any apparent justification, could subsequently be recommended to head a significantly larger and more prominent high court.
 
In another instance, he referred to a judge who had been transferred from the parent high court on punitive considerations but was later appointed chief justice of a prominent high court.
 
The former CJI expressed disappointment that appointments and transfers were being made without adequate regard to diversity, inclusion, and merit, with other irrelevant considerations allegedly influencing decisions.
 
Invoking Article 124(2) of the Constitution, Gavai said the primacy accorded to Collegium recommendations did not absolve the President of constitutional responsibilities. He maintained that the executive remained an equal stakeholder in appointments and transfers of judges to constitutional courts.
 
Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India governs the appointment, tenure, and resignation of judges of the Supreme Court of India.
 
He urged President Murmu to intervene and ensure that the judiciary remained committed to equal representation, describing it as one of the fundamental pillars of Indian democracy.
 
Copies of the letter were also sent to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal.

data.title: RBI urges banks to expedite MSME lending, reduce reliance on collateral
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has urged banks to expedite credit sanctions to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and reduce their reliance on collateral, encouraging cash-flow-based lending through digital channels to improve access to finance for the sector.
 
At the 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) on MSME credit in Kolkata, Deputy Governor Swaminathan J called for greater use of the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and other digital channels to facilitate lending to MSMEs, the RBI said in a press release.
 
He also emphasised the need to expand the use of the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) for receivables financing and strengthen early identification and resolution of stress among MSME borrowers.
 
 
The meeting reviewed the flow of working capital and investment credit to MSMEs, lending to first-time borrowers, and credit guarantee coverage. Discussions also covered the enhanced limit for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises, settlement of invoices of central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) through TReDS, and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026.
 
Recognising the contribution of MSMEs to India's economic growth and development goals, the deputy governor also called on industry associations to actively participate in the RBI's outreach initiatives, including town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings.
 
Such engagements would help improve awareness of credit-related initiatives and enable industry associations to raise concerns of their members with banks, according to the RBI.
 
The meeting was attended by representatives of the Ministry of MSME, the Department of Financial Services, select banks, Sidbi, Nabard, CGTMSE, NCGTC, KVIC, the Indian Banks' Association, and national, regional, and state-level MSME associations.

data.title: 'Make in Uttar Pradesh' push: Investors to get ₹8.5K crore in incentives
data.description:
To catalyse the ‘Make in UP’ theme, the Uttar Pradesh (UP) government will disburse almost ₹8,500 crore to private investors as incentives.
 
The incentives are for various projects set up under industry-native policies through the UP Industrial Investment & Employment Promotion Policy 2022, UP FDI/FCI, Fortune Global 500 & India 500 Policy 2023, and the UP Oxygen Production Policy 2021.
 
So far, the state government has already distributed about ₹3,500 crore as incentives, which is nearly 41 per cent of the promised incentives.
 
“The state will disburse more than ₹2,600 crore as incentives in the next few weeks, which would increase our incentive payment ratio to 71 per cent,” a senior UP official said.
 
 
The UP industry department gets the largest chunk of the incentives at ₹5,520 crore, of which nearly ₹2,421 crore or 44 per cent has been paid.
 
The Uttar Pradesh New & Renewable Energy Development Agency (UPNEDA) and the UP MSME (micro, small and medium enterprises) department have clocked the best incentive payment ratio of 48 per cent each.
 
UPNEDA will pay ₹1,650 crore as incentives to investors, of which ₹787 crore has been disbursed.
 
The UP MSME department has paid roughly ₹69 crore, of the total ₹145 crore.
 
Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister (CM) Yogi Adityanath said his government has nurtured an investment-friendly environment. An array of incentives, tax concessions, and subsidies are being extended to investors.
 
Chairing a meeting of the UP State Transformation Commission (STC) in Lucknow recently, he directed officials to ensure that infrastructure and industrial projects are completed within timelines while maintaining quality standards.
 
Officials said the tendering process for the Chitrakoot Link Expressway will be finalised by November end, while 91 per cent of the land acquisition for the Farrukhabad Link Expressway has been completed.
 
Similarly, the state government has acquired 83 per cent of the land needed for the Agra-Lucknow to Purvanchal Link Expressway, 86 per cent for the Jhansi Link Expressway and 83 per cent for the Jewar Link Expressway.
 
Letters of Award have been issued to firms selected for the construction of all three projects.
 
In addition, the verification process for the Meerut-Haridwar Expressway, Vindhya Expressway and Vindhya-Purvanchal Spur Link has been completed.
 
The CM ordered the opening of financial bids for the Multi-Modal Logistics Hub in Greater Noida within the next two weeks, and to expedite the work on the Multi-Modal Logistics Park.

data.title: HEG lists independently, plans ₹650 crore graphite electrode expansion
data.description:
HEG Limited, an LNJ Bhilwara Group company, on Friday listed its equity shares independently on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE), following the demerger of its graphite electrode business, as it plans to invest ₹650 crore to expand manufacturing capacity at its Mandideep facility in Madhya Pradesh.
 
The company will increase its annual graphite electrode manufacturing capacity from 100,000 tonnes to 115,000 tonnes, with production from the expanded facility targeted to begin in the first quarter of calendar year 2028.
 
The board has approved the brownfield expansion, which will build on existing infrastructure at less than half the capital intensity of setting up a greenfield plant, the company said in a statement.
 
 
Under the arrangement, shareholders of HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly HEG Limited) whose names appeared on the register as of September 7, 2026, received one fully paid-up equity share of HEG Limited (formerly HEG Graphite Limited), with a face value of ₹2, for every share of the same face value held in the erstwhile company.
 
HEG operates the world's largest single-site ultra-high-power (UHP) graphite electrode manufacturing facility at Mandideep, with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes. It exports around 65-70 per cent of its production to more than 35 countries and supplies several leading global steelmakers.
 
"Today HEG Limited begins trading as an independently listed company, but the business our shareholders own is the one they have known for nearly fifty years. The same plant, the same people and the same customer relationships now sit within a company focused entirely on graphite electrodes," said Ravi Jhunjhunwala, chairman, managing director, and chief executive officer of HEG Limited.
 
The company said its manufacturing scale and location provide it with the cost competitiveness to navigate business cycles. It also operates an 18 MW captive hydroelectric plant in Tawa and a 6 MW solar plant in Mandideep, which provide power for its energy-intensive manufacturing process.
 
Graphite electrodes are essential consumables in electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking. According to the company, EAF steelmaking generates approximately one-fourth of the carbon emissions associated with the blast furnace route.
 
The global shift towards lower-carbon steelmaking, driven by economics, regulation, and the need to reduce emissions, is expected to support demand for graphite electrodes. More than 100 million tonnes of new EAF steelmaking capacity is scheduled to come on stream outside China by 2030, the company said.
 
However, the company said supply cannot respond as easily to the anticipated demand, adding that no new company outside China has entered the graphite electrode industry since 1976.
 
“The listing gives shareholders a direct stake in one of the world's leading graphite electrode businesses, with its own identity and its own capital priorities,” said Riju Jhunjhunwala, vice-chairman of HEG Limited.

data.title: 136 vessels of Indian interest impacted in troubled waters since March
data.description:
Wars and piracy in global waters have affected 136 vessels of Indian interests in the past eight months, leading to the deaths of 16 Indian seafarers while five remain missing and 34 have been injured, a Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) report has said.
 
The DGMA’s latest security report covers attacks and other incidents on three major routes between March 1 and November 1. The routes are the Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman, the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Bab-el-Mandeb, and the Black Sea.
 
The Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman region accounted for 93 affected vessels, including six Indian-flagged and 87 foreign-flagged vessels, with 11 fatalities, three missing crew members, and 27 injuries reported.
 
 
In the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Bab-el-Mandeb region, six vessels were affected while the Black Sea recorded incidents involving 37 foreign-flagged vessels, resulting in five fatalities, two missing crew members, and six injuries.
 
Overall, the data highlights the significant impact of geopolitical tensions and maritime security threats on commercial shipping and the safety of Indian and foreign seafarers, the DGMA said.
 
11 seafarers still under captivity
The DGMA report also shows that 11 Indian seafarers who were aboard a vessel captured by pirates are still held captive along with 11 foreign seafarers. These seafarers were aboard the MT Asana, which was captured on July 17.
 
The data shows that 46 Indian seafarers have so far been impacted by piracy in the last eight months.
 
Seven incidents related to piracy, hijacking and armed robbery involving vessels with Indian crew members are reflected in the data, the DGMA said.
 
The remaining vessels, except the MT Asana, have been released, have resumed their voyages, or have reported the safe release of their crew, the maritime regulator’s report said.
 
Attacks in war-stricken waters have become a major concern for the government and maritime stakeholders, and seafarer unions have called for a stop to the targeting of commercial vessels.

data.title: Credai seeks affordable housing reforms, tax relief ahead of FY28 Budget
data.description:
The Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (Credai), an industry body representing private real estate developers, has sought reforms to align the definition of affordable housing with current market conditions and improve affordability for homebuyers, among its several suggestions to the finance ministry ahead of the Union Budget 2027-28.
 
Credai said in a statement on Friday that it had also sought enhanced access to housing finance through tax benefits and a reduction in long-term capital gains tax on land and buildings to support sustained investment in the sector, adding that it had shared these recommendations with the ministry during the pre-Budget consultations with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on November 20.
 
 
The recommendations come against the backdrop of a continued decline in the supply of affordable housing. The share of homes priced below ₹50 lakh across the top eight cities fell from 54 per cent in 2018 to 21 per cent in 2025, the statement showed. This decline reflects the growing affordability challenge amid rising land and construction costs, it added.
 
Separately, data from real estate consultancy Anarock showed that the share of housing supply priced below ₹40 lakh declined from 26 per cent to 10 per cent during the first nine months of 2026.
 
Credai President Shekar Patel said the body's demands for reforms in affordable housing came amid India's expanding housing requirements due to urbanisation and continued strong demand for affordable housing.
 
“There is a need to revisit the existing affordable housing definition to align it with evolving market realities. Tax thresholds need to reflect current property and construction costs,” Patel added.
 
The body has proposed a uniform, area-based definition of affordable housing across goods and services tax (GST), income tax, and priority sector lending. It has recommended limits based on Rera carpet area of 70 square metres (sq m) in notified metros, 90 sq m in urban centres with a population of 10 lakh and above, and 120 sq m elsewhere.
 
If a price ceiling is required for income tax purposes, Credai has recommended raising it to ₹90 lakh, with an annual escalation of 5 per cent to account for inflation and rising raw material and labour costs, the statement said.
 
To improve project viability, the association has sought the reintroduction of the incentive under the former Section 80-IBA through a new Section 142A. The proposal provides for a 100 per cent deduction on profits from eligible projects approved between April 2027 and March 2032. It also seeks to extend the benefit to companies, firms, and limited liability partnerships (LLPs), with exemptions from minimum alternate tax (MAT) and alternate minimum tax (AMT).
 
For homebuyers, Credai has recommended enhancing the tax deduction on housing loan interest for first-time homebuyers under the proposed affordable housing definition. The association has also proposed extending this benefit under both the old and new income tax regimes to improve affordability and encourage homeownership.
 
Further, to expand access to formal housing finance, Credai has proposed strengthening the credit guarantee mechanism for affordable home loans. This includes revising and increasing the existing loan ceiling of ₹20 lakh in line with prevailing market conditions and property rates, with a uniform 75 per cent guarantee cover. Eligibility should be linked to the value of the house rather than the borrower's income category, it said.
 
Credai has also proposed a 10-year income tax exemption on rental income from eligible affordable homes, subject to specified conditions relating to tenancy and vacancy. The measure is aimed at encouraging investment in formal rental housing and increasing the availability of affordable homes in urban centres.
 
A key recommendation is to reduce long-term capital gains tax on land and buildings held for two years or more to 5 per cent, applicable to all taxpayers, including non-residents. The proposal is intended to lower the tax burden on land transactions and encourage landowners to bring land into the development market, particularly through joint development arrangements.
 
The association has also proposed a uniform 5 per cent tax rate on other long-term capital gains and dividend income, subject to specified holding periods and tax provisions. For businesses, it has sought an optional 22 per cent tax regime for partnership firms and LLPs that forgo exemptions, bringing their tax treatment closer to that available to companies.
 
Credai has also recommended a 15 per cent tax rate for new service-sector units established in special economic zones (SEZs) between April 2027 and March 2031, with the benefit available for 10 years. The proposal is aimed at improving the competitiveness of SEZs in attracting new service-sector investment.
 
“Our recommendations seek to address these constraints through targeted fiscal measures that can improve affordability for buyers, make projects viable and encourage the release of land for development. A more consistent tax framework for housing will also support employment, investment and planned urban growth,” Patel said.

data.title: Niti Aayog weighs measures to reduce import dependence in capital goods
data.description:
Amid growing use of trade restrictions on critical components by countries, NITI Aayog is assessing India’s import dependence in the capital goods sector and preparing policy recommendations to reduce it and expand the country’s share in global supply chains.
 
According to people familiar with the matter, the recommendations are likely to focus largely on regulatory and institutional measures. Officials have sought inputs on bottlenecks that could be eased to encourage domestic manufacturing of capital goods.
 
“There are two types of dependence. One, where there is complete dependence on other countries for capital goods, and another where a large majority of the manufacturing happens here but crucial components come from countries like China, which know exactly where each critical component they are exporting stands in the global supply chain, and use export controls as leverage. NITI is looking at both these aspects,” an official said.
 
 
The exercise comes amid growing calls from the government to strengthen self-reliance and domestic manufacturing. At the Ficci Annual General Meeting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi identified hand tools, power tools and machinery manufacturing, all part of the capital goods sector, as areas with significant export potential, particularly in developing countries and the Global South.
 
NITI Aayog is likely to prepare a report as part of its trade assessment exercise. Queries sent to the think tank remained unanswered at the time of publication.
 
The exercise gains significance amid recent export restrictions announced by China on critical construction equipment such as tunnel boring machines (TBMs), which India needs for major infrastructure projects across highways, railways, metros and the energy sector.
 
On Wednesday, the Cabinet announced an ₹11,000 crore scheme to support domestic manufacturing of heavy construction equipment and develop an ecosystem for this segment of the capital goods industry.
 
While NITI Aayog has sought stakeholder inputs, the think tank is learnt to be less inclined towards financial incentives such as tax breaks and manufacturing subsidies. Instead, it is looking at ways to encourage research and development (R&D), a key area of concern across sectors.
 
The Ministry of Heavy Industries has been implementing the National Capital Goods Policy for a decade, with its second phase currently underway. Under the ₹1,207 crore Phase II programme, 29 projects have been sanctioned, including centres of excellence, common engineering facilities, testing and certification centres, and technology accelerators.
 
The FY27 Budget also proposed two hi-tech tool rooms to support domestic design, testing and production of high-precision components.
 
A report last week by the Confederation of Indian Industry and Boston Consulting Group called for greater focus on capital goods in emerging sectors such as semiconductors and data centres. It suggested extending selected incentive benefits, including those under the Semicon India Programme, to domestic capital goods development and procurement, backed by phased, product-specific domestic value addition thresholds verified through factory audits.
 
The report also called for a review of inverted duty structures, where finished equipment used in electronics manufacturing attracts lower duties than the inputs and sub-assemblies required to manufacture it domestically.
 
“The government could also review duty inversions where, for instance, finished equipment used in electronics manufacturing attracts lower duty than inputs and sub-assemblies needed to make it domestically. Any resulting structural cost disadvantage for domestic manufacturers could be addressed by aligning duties on identified inputs,” it said.
 
The report also recommended incentives for R&D and measures to bridge the financing gap between Indian manufacturers and global peers.
 
India has an import dependence of 38 per cent or more in seven of the 10 capital goods sub-sectors, according to the report. In three sub-sectors, plastic processing, machine tools and textile machinery, import dependence ranges between 59 per cent and 67 per cent.

data.title: Sebi grants Tata Steel extension till Dec 8 for APL Apollo Tubes open offer
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Friday granted Tata Steel an extension until December 8 to publish the detailed statement for its open offer to acquire up to a 26 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes, the company said in an exchange filing.
 
The detailed public statement was earlier required to be published by December 1. The extension was granted through an email by Sebi on Friday, following a request submitted by Tata Steel, the filing noted.
 
The extension comes amid concerns raised by proxy advisers, institutional investors, and other shareholders over the deal.
 
However, the deadline for filing the draft letter of offer with Sebi remains unchanged at December 8, 2026, the filing added.
 
 
The company’s management had earlier noted that it would be revising the contours of the deal.
